problem:
Given that $n=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, find a unit vector that is parallel to $n.$

|  |  | $-\frac{2}{3}$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $u=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  |
|  |  | {{field-2}} |  |
worked_solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
u=\frac{n}{|\,n\,|}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,n\,| & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $n$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{n}{|\,n\,|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}n \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
